name: H5N1 bird flu
value: 3 cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: Three Yakima County H5N1 cases in 2026, all linked to infected dairy cattle, one fatal; no human-to-human spread
state: Yakima County, Washington, reported two human H5N1 cases on 31 Oct and 1 Nov, one of them fatal, making three in the county in 2026; both had exposure to infected dairy cattle (UKHSA, 5 Nov). The CDC counts 72 confirmed human H5 cases in the US since 2024, and local authorities rate the risk to the public as low. Searches to 10 Nov found no newer human case or cluster, so these remain animal-to-human cases.
for_you: Risk to the public is low. People who work with poultry or dairy cattle should follow UKHSA or CDC guidance on protective equipment and report flu-like symptoms after exposure.
rubric_hit: Sporadic animal-to-human cases only (3 Yakima cases, dairy exposure); no human clusters

sources.title: UKHSA — Outbreaks under monitoring: week 44 (week ending 1 November 2026)

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.

rubric.watch: Human clusters under investigation, rising human cases, or new mammalian species spread.
